    Who reads it

    Built for the people who work the deal.

    If a rezoning next door changes your listing, your lot pipeline, your case or your collateral, you want it the week it's filed. Not when the sign goes up.

    • Brokers

      See what's being rezoned near your listings and your farm area, before the sign goes up.

      "What just got filed on that corner?"
    • Builders & developers

      Watch the plats coming through and see where new lots are going in your submarket.

      "What's being platted near Five Forks?"
    • Land-use attorneys

      Keep up with your matters and the ones across the table, including the ones that get carried over.

      "Is that variance back on the docket?"
    • Lenders & appraisers

      Catch a zoning change next to the collateral before it shows up in someone else's report.

      "What's going in next door?"

    Why it matters

    Before it's built, it's filed.

    Most projects in the county go through a public hearing long before anyone breaks ground. The filing is public record. It's also buried in a meeting PDF most people never open.

      Stop digging through county PDFs.

      Hold your spot now. It's free, and the $149 founding rate is yours if you decide to start.

      Reserve my spot →

      What's covered?

      Greenville County's Planning Commission, Board of Zoning Appeals and Subdivision Advisory Committee. Coming next: Anderson County, plus the boards of the City of Greenville and the county's other cities. Founding members get each one as it's added, at the same rate.

      When does the first issue go out?

      As soon as our listings pass accuracy checks against the county's own agendas. We'll email you first, and you won't be charged until you choose to start.

      What does reserving commit me to?

      Nothing. It holds your place and the founding rate. You can say no when we email you.

      Is this from the county?

      No. Parsed Agendas is independent and not affiliated with Greenville County. Everything comes from the county's public agendas, as printed.

      Is it legal or appraisal advice?

      No. It's a record of public filings that saves you the reading. Check anything that matters against the county's documents.

      Who's behind it?

      Timothy Sevilla, founder, and Matt Buchanan, co-founder, here in the Upstate. Parsed Agendas reads the county's agendas so you don't have to.
